newsitem.title: INDIA: India's pepper exchange to go on stream in August.
newsitem.headline: India's pepper exchange to go on stream in August.

text.p: India's first international futures exchange for pepper is expected to be operational by the middle of August, an official of the Indian Pepper and Spices Trade Association (IPSTA) said on Friday.
"The target date is mid-August," IPSTA president T. Vidyasagar told Reuters by telephone from the southern Indian city of Cochin.
Vidyasagar said the exchange had been conducting trial runs for the past fortnight and continously checking the systems.
"Trading will be by open outcry," he said.
He said certain procedural issues pending with the finance ministry on repatriation of funds were likely to be ironed out in the next few days. "We are more or less ready."
Procedural snags had delayed India's ambitious plans to start the exchange by the end of April.
In February, the Food Ministry announced that the country's first international exchange and clearing house for pepper would start functioning at Kochi.
India's cabinet decided in the second half of 1995 to upgrade the domestic futures commodity exchange, run by IPSTA into an international exchange.
The domestic exchange has 140 members and the annual volume of trade is about six billion rupees ($168 million).
"We have already 52 applications for the international division from domestic traders," Vidyasagar said.
He said IPSTA would extend it to foreign players several of whom had already shown interest.
"Unless our slate is clear, we cannot tell them," he said.

A government statement in April said five million rupees had been collected from members enrolled for trading at the international exchange towards equity capital of the First Commodity Clearing Corporation of India (FCCI).
Commercial banks were seeking permission from the Reserve Bank of India to contribute to the equity capital of the clearing corporation, it said.
Vidyasagar said eight private and state-run banks were seeking permission from the Reserve Bank of India to contribute to the equity capital.
"It has taken 18 months for the start of the exchange, it is not at all a long time," said Vidyasagar. "It is well within reach."
